results.reason: Issue 3 cites SA § 2.2 with automatic five-year Renewal Terms and the 270/240-day notice window. It calls this effectively a 30-day window and says missing it locks Harrowgate in for five more years.

Issue 4 quotes § 3.1 'all glass and PET containers for any beverage product ... worldwide'. It contrasts this with the Term Sheet's amber glass bottles for beer brands at U.S./Canadian facilities and states the executed text controls.

Issue 1 cites Recital C's August 3, 2026 receipt date and computes expiry on September 2, 2026, 19 days before the September 21 Amendment. It concludes the increase is deemed accepted absent an extension or waiver.

Issue 2 states Amendment § 2 replaces § 11.2, deletes the Recall carve-out and limits the indemnity carve-out to third-party IP claims under § 9.1(c). It explains recall and product-liability exposure is now capped at six months of fees.

Issue 5 describes new § 14.4 allowing assignment 'without the consent of Customer' to Affiliates or successors, overriding § 14.3. It notes there is no competitor exclusion and that the restriction is now one-sided.
The Summary states that under SA § 15.2 written amendments come first and that the Amendment controls where it conflicts with the SA.
The response quotes § 11.1's cap as 'the fees paid by Customer in the six months before the claim arose.'
The memo is addressed to the Supervising Partner and lists issues one by one. Each issue has a Location and a Recommended fix section.
The response proposes specific language for all five issues, including a restored § 11.2, a narrowed § 3.1, a revised § 2.2 and a competitor exclusion in § 14.4.
The response states the window has closed and Harrowgate cannot now serve a timely objection. It seeks an express extension or waiver.
The response states the Term Sheet is non-binding and superseded, and that Harrowgate is bound by the broader § 3.1.
